quotes.text: A steady pace still gets there.
Small progress is still progress.
Start where you are; use what you have.
Today gets easier when you take the next step.
Breathe in. Reset. Continue.
Quiet moments count too.
Peace can be a plan.
Soft starts are still starts.
Home is built from tiny acts of care.
The best days leave room for each other.
Little traditions become big memories.
This house runs on love and snacks.
You don't have to see the whole staircase, just the next step.
Rest is part of the work, not a break from it.
Do the next right thing; the rest follows.
A calm morning is a gift you give the day.
Kindness costs nothing and returns more than it asks.
The day is yours to shape, one small choice at a time.
Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast.
What you do today echoes into tomorrow.
You are allowed to go slowly.
Do a small kindness you do not have to.
A tidy corner is a small, quiet victory.
Gratitude is the shortest road to a good mood.
A warm hello can carry a whole day.
Finish one thing and the rest finds its shape.
Water, rest, and patience are not laziness.
Small steps taken daily go a very long way.
The house breathes easier when the mind does.
“All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players.” — William Shakespeare
“It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.” — Charles Dickens
“Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.” — Oscar Wilde
“We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.” — Oscar Wilde
“Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.” — Martin Luther King Jr.
“There is no greater agony than bearing an untold story inside you.” — Maya Angelou
“Go confidently in the direction of your dreams.” — Henry David Thoreau
“A room without books is like a body without a soul.” — Cicero
“Imagination is more important than knowledge.” — Albert Einstein
“Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication.” — Leonardo da Vinci
“However long the night, the day is sure to come.” — Rabindranath Tagore
“The secret of getting ahead is getting started.” — Mark Twain
“Well begun is half done.” — Aristotle
“In the end, it is not the years in your life, but the life in your years.” — Abraham Lincoln

jokes.text: Why did the calendar feel popular? It had a lot of dates.
I only know 25 letters of the alphabet. I don't know y.
Why did the scarecrow win? He was outstanding in his field.
Parallel lines have so much in common. It is a shame they'll never meet.
Why did the bicycle fall over? It was two-tired.
What do clouds wear under their shorts? Thunderwear.
Why can't your nose be twelve inches long? Then it would be a foot.
What did one wall say to the other? I'll meet you at the corner.
I told my wife she was drawing her eyebrows too high. She looked surprised.
Why don't scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything.
I'm reading a book about anti-gravity. It's impossible to put down.
What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta.
Why did the coffee file a police report? It got mugged.
I used to be a banker, but I lost interest.
What's the best thing about Switzerland? I don't know, but the flag is a big plus.
Why did the math book look sad? It had too many problems.
What did the grape do when it got stepped on? It let out a little whine.
Why did the picture go to jail? Because it was framed.
What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear.
Why did the tomato blush? Because it saw the salad dressing.
What do you call cheese that is not yours? Nacho cheese.
I would tell you a joke about construction, but I am still working on it.
Why don't eggs tell jokes? They would crack each other up.
What did the ocean say to the beach? Nothing, it just waved.
Why did the golfer bring two pairs of pants? In case he got a hole in one.
I used to think I was indecisive. Now I am not so sure.
Why did the robot go on a diet? It had too much disk space.

facts.text: Honey never spoils when stored properly.
Bananas are berries, botanically speaking.
Octopuses have three hearts.
A day on Venus is longer than a Venus year.
Sound travels faster in water than in air.
Water expands when it freezes.
Lightning can heat nearby air hotter than the Sun's surface.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth.
Wombat droppings are roughly cube-shaped.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
The shortest war in history lasted about 38 minutes.
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
Sea otters hold hands while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
In summer, the Eiffel Tower can grow up to about 15 cm taller as the metal expands.
The human brain uses roughly 20 percent of the body's energy while taking up only 2 percent of its weight.
A blue whale's heart can weigh about 180 kilograms, roughly the size of a small golf cart.
Tigers have striped skin, not just striped fur.
A group of owls is called a parliament.
The smallest bone in the human body is the stapes in the ear.
A day on Neptune lasts about sixteen Earth hours.
Elephants can recognize themselves in a mirror.
A group of lions is called a pride.
A giraffe's tongue can be about 45 centimeters long.
A hummingbird's heart can beat up to 1,200 times per minute.
The first computer mouse was a wooden box.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest structure built by living things.
The Sun makes up about 99.8 percent of the solar system's mass.
A day on Jupiter lasts about ten hours.
The deepest point in the ocean is the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench.
Sharks have been on Earth for more than 400 million years.
The sciatic nerve is the longest nerve in the human body.
Honeybees can recognize human faces.
The rafflesia is the largest flower in the world.
Flamingos feed with their heads upside down.
Light travels about 300,000 kilometers per second.
More than 60 percent of Earth's fresh water is stored as ice.
Coral is an animal, not a plant.
A newborn blue whale is about 2.5 meters long.
Saturn is less dense than water.
The first computer email was the two letters 'ahb'.
Some snails can hibernate for up to three years.
The human stomach renews its lining every few days.
Strawberries carry their seeds on the outside.
Penguins choose a mate with a pebble.
Diamond and pencil lead are both made of carbon.
The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land combined.

riddles.text: What has hands but cannot clap? A clock.
What gets wetter as it dries? A towel.
What has many keys but opens no locks? A piano.
What has a head, a tail, and no body? A coin.
What can travel around the world while staying in a corner? A stamp.
What has words but never speaks? A book.
What has a bed but never sleeps? A river.
What has a neck but no head? A bottle.
What goes up but never comes down? Your age.
What can fill a room but takes up no space? Light.
What has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish? A map.
What has teeth but cannot bite? Answer: A comb.
What has an eye but cannot see? Answer: A needle.
The more you take, the more you leave behind. Answer: Footsteps.
What comes down but never goes up? Answer: Rain.
What has a heart that does not beat? Answer: An artichoke.
What can you catch but not throw? Answer: A cold.
What has a bottom but no top? Answer: A bottomless pit.
What breaks the moment you say its name? Answer: Silence.
What has four legs in the morning, two at noon, and three at night? Answer: A person.
What gets bigger the more you take away? Answer: A hole.
What has a thumb and four fingers but is not alive? Answer: A glove.

trivia.text: What is the largest planet in our solar system? Answer: Jupiter.
What is the largest ocean on Earth? Answer: The Pacific Ocean.
How many continents are there? Answer: Seven.
How many inches are in a foot? Answer: Twelve.
At what temperature does water freeze in Fahrenheit? Answer: 32 degrees.
How many legs does a spider have? Answer: Eight.
Which gas do plants take in to make food? Answer: Carbon dioxide.
What is the tallest mountain above sea level? Answer: Mount Everest.
How many minutes are in an hour? Answer: Sixty.
How many days are in a leap year? Answer: 366.
What is the chemical formula for water? Answer: H2O.
How many players does a soccer team field? Answer: Eleven.
What is the largest mammal on Earth? Answer: The blue whale.
How many sides does a hexagon have? Answer: Six.
What is the smallest planet in our solar system? Answer: Mercury.
What is the only mammal that can truly fly? Answer: The bat.
How many strings does a standard guitar have? Answer: Six.
What is the national bird of the United States? Answer: The bald eagle.
Which metal is liquid at room temperature? Answer: Mercury.
What is the tallest animal on Earth? Answer: The giraffe.
How many colors are in a rainbow? Answer: Seven.
What is the hardest natural substance on Earth? Answer: Diamond.
Which instrument has 88 keys? Answer: The piano.
What is the largest bird in the world? Answer: The ostrich.
How many bones are in the adult human body? Answer: 206.
What is the smallest country in the world? Answer: Vatican City.
Which planet is known as the Red Planet? Answer: Mars.
What is the fastest bird in a dive? Answer: The peregrine falcon.
What is the average length of a human pregnancy in weeks? Answer: About forty.
Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe? Answer: Nitrogen.

compliments.text: You make this house feel like a harbor.
The room is brighter when you walk in.
You are the reason the table is never empty.
Your laugh is the best sound in this house.
You turn ordinary mornings into something to look forward to.
Someone in this family is very lucky to have you.
You remember the small things, and it matters.
The way you care is the kind of thing people talk about.
You are steady, and steady is a superpower.
Your patience makes everyone around you calmer.
You make hard days feel shareable.
The kitchen feels warmer when you are in it.
You are the glue that keeps this crew together.
Your kindness lands quietly and lasts all day.
The house runs smoother because you show up.
You bring good luck just by being here.
Your curiosity keeps this family learning.
You are the one people come to when they need a straight answer.
The world is a little kinder because you are in it.
You make everyone around you a little braver.
The best part of any week is the table you set.
You are the calm in this house's storm.
Your work shows up in the little things you fix.
The people you love are better for knowing you.
